title: Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards: government response to report
description: The government's response to the Committee's 2020 report Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards
summary: The government is responding to the Committee's 2020 report on AI and Public Standards, outlining its commitment to strengthen regulation, safety, and transparency in artificial intelligence. It proposes clearer guidelines for developers, accountability frameworks, and closer collaboration with industry to ensure responsible AI deployment.

title: ​​Ofqual’s approach to regulating the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector​
description: Published in response to a request from the Secretary of State for Education, the Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology, and the Secretary of State for Business and Trade.
summary: Ofqual outlines how it will oversee the use of artificial intelligence in setting and assessing qualifications, aiming to keep exams fair and reliable. The guidance focuses on clear rules for developers, examiners and candidates to ensure AI tools are used safely and transparently.

title: Report and impact assessment on Copyright and Artificial Intelligence
description: A report and impact assessment on the use of copyright works in the development of artificial intelligence (AI) systems.
summary: The report examines how copyrighted material is used when training and deploying artificial intelligence systems. It assesses the legal, ethical, and economic impacts of this practice and offers recommendations to balance innovation with protection of creators' rights.

title: Government response to the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence
description: Government response to the Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence report ‘AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency’.
summary: The UK government has released a formal response to the House of Lords Select Committee’s report, “AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency,” outlining its strategy to balance AI innovation with safety and ethical concerns. It promises to strengthen regulatory frameworks, invest in research, and promote international collaboration while ensuring the technology benefits all citizens.

title: AI and Public Standards – Terms of Reference
description: Terms of Reference and FAQs for the Committee's review into artificial intelligence and public standards.
summary: This document sets out the terms of reference for a committee that will examine how artificial intelligence should fit within public standards, and includes a list of frequently asked questions to guide the discussion. It explains the committee's purpose, scope, expected outcomes, and the main issues it will address to help align AI practices with societal expectations.

title: CSPL submission to Science and Technology Committee inquiry on Governance of AI
description: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry on Governance of Artificial Intelligence.
summary: CSPL has provided written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee’s inquiry into the governance of artificial intelligence. In its submission, the organisation outlines concerns and recommendations regarding policy, regulation, and oversight of AI development and deployment.

title: Impact of AI on the regulation of medical products
description: Implementing the Artificial Intelligence (AI) White Paper principles.
summary: The policy explains how AI changes the rules that govern medical products, aiming to keep them safe, effective, and trustworthy. It details how to embed the AI White Paper principles into current regulations, focusing on risk assessment, data management, and regulatory oversight.

title: Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy
description: Our vision is that, in terms of AI, we will be the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted and influential Defence organisation for our size.
summary: The Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy outlines how the organisation will use AI to strengthen national security and improve defence operations. Its goal is to become the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted and influential AI‑driven defence force for its size.

title: Transport artificial intelligence action plan
description: Sets out how DfT will work with the transport sector to exploit the opportunities from AI while managing potential risks.
summary: The Transport Artificial Intelligence Action Plan explains how the Department for Transport will work with the transport sector to make the most of AI’s benefits while keeping its risks under control. It sets out strategies for innovation, safety, and regulation so that AI can be used responsibly across all modes of transport.

title: Copyright and artificial intelligence: progress report
description: A progress report on the use of copyright works in the development of AI systems, under Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act.
summary: The report reviews how copyright‑protected works are used to train AI systems under Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act, highlighting current practices and legal compliance. It outlines progress, challenges, and recommended steps for the AI industry to ensure responsible use of copyrighted material.
